compose.description: Advanced function composition primitives inspired by functional programming. Provides compose, pipe, partial application, currying, lazy evaluation, thunks, and memoization decorators.
Mathematical function composition: (f . g)(x) = f(g(x)) Returns a function definition string that can be evaluated or used with apply.

pipe_fn.description: Left-to-right function pipeline: pipe(f, g, h)(x) = h(g(f(x))) Opposite of mathematical composition - data flows left to right.

chain.description: Chain functions with error propagation - stops on first failure. Each function receives the output of the previous as input. If any function returns non-zero, the chain stops and returns that code.

partial.description: Create a new function with some arguments pre-filled. The partially applied function can be called with remaining arguments.

curry.description: Transform a multi-argument function into a chain of single-argument functions. Each call returns a new function until all arguments are provided.

flip.description: Create a new function with the first two arguments swapped. Useful for adapting binary functions for use with map/reduce.

tap.description: Create a function that executes fn for side effects but returns the original input. Useful for logging, debugging, or triggering actions in a pipeline.

identity.description: The identity function - returns its input unchanged. Useful as a default or placeholder in composition.

constant.description: Create a function that ignores its input and always returns a constant value. Useful for providing default values or terminating recursion.

apply.description: Apply a function to an array of arguments (spread operator). Converts array elements to function arguments.

lazy.description: Create a lazy thunk - a deferred computation. The function is not executed until force() is called.

force.description: Force evaluation of a lazy thunk. Results are cached - subsequent force() calls return cached value.

lazy_seq.description: Create a lazy infinite sequence from a generator function. The generator receives the current index (0-based) and should return the value.

take_lazy.description: Take n elements from a lazy sequence. Advances the sequence state so subsequent calls get next elements.

memoize_fn.description: Create a memoized version of a function using in-memory cache. Faster than disk-based memoize from cache.sh for session-local caching.

cache_clear_fn.description: Clear memoization cache for functions matching a pattern. Without pattern, clears all in-memory memo cache.

compose_reset.description: Reset all compose module state (thunks, sequences, memo cache). Useful for testing or starting fresh.

try_each.description: Create a function that tries each function in order until one succeeds. Useful for fallback chains.

when.description: Create a conditional function: applies fn only when predicate returns true. Otherwise returns input unchanged.

mainframe_confirm_risk.description: Auto-approve if the command's risk score is below the threshold. If mainframe_risk_score is available (from risk.sh), uses it for scoring. Falls back to always-ask if risk.sh is not loaded.

mainframe_confirm_batch.description: Show a batch of commands and confirm all-or-nothing. User sees the full list before making a single decision.

mainframe_confirm_timeout.description: Confirmation with a timeout. If the user does not respond within the specified number of seconds, the request is automatically denied.

mainframe_confirm_policy.description: Set the confirmation policy for subsequent operations. always - always prompt for confirmation never  - auto-approve everything (dangerous for production) risk   - use risk scoring to decide (requires risk.sh)

mainframe_confirm_threshold.description: Set the risk threshold for auto-approve in risk-based policy mode. Commands with risk scores below this threshold are auto-approved. Commands at or above this threshold require interactive confirmation.

mainframe_confirm_log.description: Show the full confirmation history as a JSON array. Each entry contains timestamp, message, decision, and method.

mainframe_confirm_count.description: Return the number of entries in the confirmation history.

mainframe_confirm_last.description: Show the most recent confirmation decision.

mainframe_confirm_auto_approve.description: Force auto-approve mode. All confirmations return 0 without prompting. Useful for CI/testing environments where interactive input is unavailable.

database.description: Pure bash wrapper around sqlite3 CLI providing connection management, prepared statement emulation, transactions, schema operations, and USOP-compliant JSON output.

db_connect.description: Open or create a SQLite database file. Sets up the connection state and applies default pragmas for performance and safety.

db_close.description: Close the current database connection. Rolls back any active transaction.

db_is_connected.description: Check if a database connection is active.

db_path.description: Get the path of the currently connected database.

db_query.description: Execute a SELECT query and return results as a JSON array of objects. Each row becomes a JSON object with column names as keys.
db_query.signature: local users=$(db_query "SELECT id, name FROM users")

db_execute.description: Execute an INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE statement. Updates the internal counters for changes() and last_insert_rowid(). If a transaction is active, statements are batched for execution at commit.
db_execute.signature: db_execute "UPDATE users SET active = 0 WHERE id = 5"

db_execute_batch.description: Execute multiple SQL statements as a batch. All statements run in a single sqlite3 invocation for efficiency. If a transaction is active, statements are added to the batch.
db_execute_batch.signature: db_execute_batch "INSERT INTO t1 VALUES (1); INSERT INTO t1 VALUES (2);"

db_query_row.description: Execute a query expecting a single row result. Returns a JSON object (not an array). Returns error if query returns zero or multiple rows.
db_query_row.signature: local user=$(db_query_row "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = 1")

db_query_value.description: Execute a query expecting a single scalar value (one row, one column). Returns just the value without JSON wrapping.

db_query_column.description: Execute a query and return a single column as a JSON array of values. Only the first column is returned if multiple columns selected.

db_prepare.description: Prepare a SQL statement with ? placeholders for later binding and execution. This emulates prepared statements by storing the SQL and replacing placeholders at execution time.
db_prepare.signature: local stmt_id=$(db_prepare "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ? AND active = ?")

db_bind.description: Bind values to a prepared statement. Values are provided in order corresponding to ? placeholders. Values are automatically escaped.

db_run_prepared.description: Execute a prepared statement with its bound values. For SELECT statements, returns JSON array. For INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, returns nothing but updates internal change counters.

db_clear_bindings.description: Clear the bound values for a prepared statement.

db_transaction_begin.description: Begin a database transaction. All subsequent operations will be grouped until commit or rollback.

db_transaction_commit.description: Commit the current transaction. All changes since BEGIN are persisted.

db_transaction_rollback.description: Rollback the current transaction. All changes since BEGIN are discarded.

db_with_transaction.description: Execute a command within a transaction. Automatically commits on success or rolls back on failure. Supports nested calls by detecting existing transactions.

db_tables.description: List all tables in the database.

db_columns.description: Get column information for a table. Returns JSON array with objects containing: cid, name, type, notnull, dflt_value, pk.

db_schema.description: Get the CREATE statement for a table.

diff_strings.description: Generate unified diff between two strings. Uses temp files internally, cleans up after.

diff_files.description: Generate unified diff between two files.

diff_preview.description: Generate diff between a file and new content (preview changes).

diff_replace_string.description: Replace text in a string. Handles multiline.

diff_stats.description: Count changes in a unified diff.

docker_running.description: Check if Docker daemon is running

mainframe_dryrun_enabled.description: Check whether dry-run mode is currently enabled.

mainframe_plan_show.description: Display the current plan in the specified format.

mainframe_plan_clear.description: Clear all recorded plan steps and reset the counter.

mainframe_plan_count.description: Print the number of currently recorded plan steps.

mainframe_plan_execute.description: Execute the recorded plan. With --confirm, displays the plan and waits for user confirmation before proceeding. With --step N, executes only that step. With --continue-on-error, does not abort on first failure.

mainframe_plan_export.description: Export the plan to a file or stdout. Uses MAINFRAME_PLAN_FORMAT for formatting.

mainframe_plan_remove.description: Remove a specific step from the plan by its step number.

mainframe_plan_reorder.description: Move a step from one position to another, shifting other steps accordingly.

mainframe_plan_risk_summary.description: Show aggregate risk information: total score, max score, and distribution across risk levels. Useful for approval gates.

mainframe_plan_results.description: Display the success/failure status of each executed step.

dryrun_exec.description: Execute a command, or record it if in dry-run mode.

embed_cache_get.description: Get cached embedding by text hash.

embed_text.description: Generate embedding vector for text content. Uses caching to avoid redundant API calls.

embed_batch.description: Batch embed lines from a file. Each line is embedded separately and output as JSONL.

embed_similarity.description: Calculate cosine similarity between two embedding vectors.

embed_dimensions.description: Get embedding dimensions for a provider/model.

embed_providers.description: Check which embedding providers are available.

error::has_error.description: Check if there's an error set

error::on_exit.description: Register a cleanup function to run on exit

forensics.description: Deep error context capture, stack traces, variable snapshots, and error chains for debugging multi-agent AI systems. Produces USOP JSON output for automated analysis.

forensics_stack.description: Get the current call stack as a formatted string. Each frame shows function name, file, and line number.

forensics_stack_json.description: Get the current call stack as a JSON array. Each frame includes func, file, and line keys.

forensics_caller.description: Get caller information at a specific stack depth. Depth 1 = immediate caller, 2 = caller's caller, etc.

forensics_capture.description: Capture the current execution context including call stack, local variables, and selected environment variables.

forensics_snapshot.description: Create a named snapshot of the current execution state. Snapshots can be compared later with forensics_diff.

forensics_diff.description: Compare two snapshots and return the differences. Shows added, removed, and changed variables.

forensics_error.description: Create an error with optional cause linking to form a chain. Error chains help trace the root cause through multiple layers.

forensics_chain_add.description: Add a new error to an existing error chain. Use this to wrap errors as they propagate up the call stack.

forensics_chain_dump.description: Dump the full error chain starting from a specific error. If no error ID provided, dumps all errors in the chain.

forensics_root_cause.description: Find the root cause by following the cause chain. Returns the first error in the chain (deepest cause).

forensics_watch.description: Start watching a variable for changes. Changes are recorded with timestamps for debugging.

forensics_watched_changes.description: Get all recorded changes for watched variables. Returns array of {var, timestamp, action, value} objects.

forensics_bundle_save.description: Save a complete forensic bundle to a file. File format is JSON with USOP metadata.

forensics_bundle_load.description: Load and display a forensic bundle from file. Outputs formatted summary to stdout.

forensics_trap_install.description: Install an error trap that automatically captures forensic context when errors occur. Bundles are saved to MAINFRAME_FORENSICS_DIR.

forensics_clear.description: Clear all forensics state (error chains, watches, snapshots).

forensics_status.description: Get status of the forensics system.

is_not_empty.description: Check if string is not empty

future_await.description: Block until a future completes or times out Returns as soon as the future transitions to done, failed, or cancelled

future_exit_code.description: Get the exit code of a completed future

future_run_v.description: Run command and store future ID in variable (avoids subshell)

future_exit_code_v.description: Get exit code into variable (avoids subshell)

fuzzy.description: Comprehensive fuzzy string matching, edit distances, phonetic encoding, and approximate search algorithms in pure bash.

levenshtein_distance.description: Calculate the Levenshtein distance (minimum single-character edits: insertions, deletions, or substitutions) to transform s1 into s2.

levenshtein_similarity.description: Calculate similarity as a ratio. 1.0 = identical, 0.0 = completely different.

damerau_levenshtein.description: Like Levenshtein but also counts transpositions of adjacent characters as a single edit (e.g., "ab" -> "ba" has distance 1, not 2).

hamming_distance.description: Counts the number of positions at which the corresponding characters differ. Only valid for strings of equal length.

jaro_distance.description: Jaro similarity accounts for transpositions and matching characters within a specific window. Higher values indicate more similarity.

jaro_winkler_distance.description: Jaro-Winkler adds a prefix bonus for strings that match from the start. The scaling factor (p) defaults to 0.1.

longest_common_substring.description: Find the longest substring that appears in both strings.

longest_common_subsequence.description: Find the longest subsequence present in both strings.

lcs_length.description: More efficient than longest_common_subsequence when you only need length.

fuzzy_match.description: Check if pattern characters appear in order in the string (fzf-style). Pattern "abc" matches "a_b_c", "abc", "aXbYcZ", etc.

fuzzy_score.description: Score based on consecutive matches, word boundaries, and positions. Uses fzf-style scoring algorithm.

fuzzy_contains.description: Like fuzzy_match but with threshold tolerance.

fuzzy_filter.description: Filter an array by fuzzy pattern, returning all matches.

fuzzy_sort.description: Sort array elements by how well they match the pattern.

fuzzy_best_match.description: Find the single best matching item in the array.

fuzzy_top_n.description: Find top N matches with their scores.

fuzzy_find_all.description: Find all matches above a similarity threshold.

fuzzy_rank.description: Rank all items by match quality.

fuzzy_search.description: Search for approximate matches in text.

fuzzy_grep.description: Fuzzy grep through lines (from stdin or arguments).

fuzzy_index_of.description: Find approximate position of pattern in string.

soundex.description: Generate Soundex code for a word. Words that sound similar produce the same code.

metaphone.description: Generate Metaphone code for a word. More accurate than Soundex for English pronunciation.

double_metaphone.description: Generate Double Metaphone codes. Provides both primary and alternate encodings for words with multiple pronunciations.

phonetic_match.description: Check if two words sound similar using phonetic encoding.

phonetic_distance.description: Calculate phonetic similarity between two words.

keyboard_distance.description: Calculate the physical distance between two keys on a QWERTY keyboard.

typo_candidates.description: Generate likely typo variants for a word (adjacent key errors, missing letters, swapped letters).

typo_suggest.description: Suggest corrections for a typo from a dictionary.

ngrams.description: Generate n-grams (substrings of length n) from a string.

ngram_similarity.description: Calculate similarity based on shared n-grams using Jaccard coefficient. similarity = |intersection| / |union|

normalize_for_fuzzy.description: Normalize a string for fuzzy matching.

fuzzy_set_threshold.description: Set the global fuzzy match threshold.

mainframe_limit_reset.description: Reset usage counters. With no argument, resets all counters. With a type argument, resets only that counter.

mainframe_limit_remaining.description: Show the remaining quota for a specific limit type. Prints "unlimited" if no limit is set (max=0).

mainframe_limit_enforce.description: Run a command only if the current limits allow it. Checks all active limits (those with max > 0) before executing. Increments the files counter by 1 after successful execution.

mainframe_limit_is_enabled.description: Check if the limits system is currently active.

llm_functions.description: Pure bash library for parsing, validating, and executing LLM tool calls. Supports both OpenAI and Anthropic formats. Provides tool registry, schema validation, and result formatting.

llm_register_tool.description: Register a tool for execution llm_register_tool "get_weather" "my_weather_func" '{ "name": "get_weather", "description": "Get weather for a city", "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": { "city": {"type": "string", "description": "City name"} }, "required": ["city"] } }'

llm_list_tools.description: List all registered tools Output: One tool name per line

llm_get_tool_schema.description: Get schema for a specific tool Output: Schema JSON

llm_tool_exists.description: Check if a tool is registered

llm_detect_format.description: Detect format of LLM response (openai or anthropic) Output: "openai", "anthropic", or "unknown"

llm_parse_tool_call.description: Parse tool call from LLM response (auto-detects format) Output: JSON object with normalized tool call info: {"id":"...", "name":"...", "arguments":{...}}

llm_parse_tool_calls.description: Parse all tool calls from response (for multiple tool calls) Output: JSON array of normalized tool calls

llm_validate_tool_args.description: Validate tool arguments against schema Note: Uses lib/schema.sh for validation when available

llm_validate_tool_args_errors.description: Get validation errors for tool arguments Output: JSON array of error messages

llm_execute_tool.description: Execute a registered tool with arguments Output: Tool execution result (raw output from function)

llm_execute_tool_safe.description: Execute tool and capture result with metadata Output: JSON with result, error, duration, etc.

llm_format_tool_result.description: Format tool result for LLM consumption Output: Formatted result JSON for OpenAI or Anthropic

llm_tools_to_openai.description: Export all tools in OpenAI function format Output: JSON array of function definitions

llm_tools_to_anthropic.description: Export all tools in Anthropic tool format Output: JSON array of tool definitions

llm_tool_export.description: Export single tool in specified format format: "openai" or "anthropic"

llm_process_tool_call.description: Process a complete tool call cycle: parse, execute, format result Output: Formatted tool result ready to send back to LLM

llm_tool_info.description: Get tool info as JSON Output: JSON with tool name, description, function, has_schema

llm_execute_tool_v.description: Execute tool and store result in variable

llm_validate_tool_args_v.description: Validate tool args and store result in variable Sets result_var to "true" or "false"

llm_providers.description: Pure bash interface for OpenAI, Anthropic, and Ollama LLM APIs. Provides consistent chat, completion, and embedding operations across providers with automatic retry, rate limiting, and USOP-compliant JSON output.

llm_anthropic_models.description: List Anthropic models (static list as API doesn't provide this)

llm_ollama_pull.description: Pull a model from Ollama registry

llm_provider_available.description: Check if a provider is available (API key set or service running)

llm_status.description: Get provider status for all providers

llm_stream.description: Pure bash streaming response handler for LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic). Parses Server-Sent Events (SSE) format, handles delta content extraction, and provides callback-based token processing with cancellation support.

llm_stream_on_token.description: Register callback for each received token

llm_stream_request.description: Start streaming request to LLM API

llm_stream_simple.description: Stream with simple text output (no callbacks needed)

llm_stream_sync.description: Synchronous stream with full response returned

llm_stream_to_usop.description: Wrap stream result in USOP envelope

llm_stream_openai_payload.description: Build OpenAI chat completion request payload

llm_tokens.description: Pure bash tokenizer library for LLM context management. Provides model-specific token counting, cost estimation, text truncation, and chunk splitting for AI agent workflows.

llm_count_tokens.description: Count tokens for text using model's tokenizer Falls back to character-based estimation if tiktoken unavailable Output: integer token count

llm_count_tokens_file.description: Count tokens in a file Output: integer token count

llm_estimate_cost.description: Estimate API cost for text based on token count Output: JSON object with cost details

llm_get_pricing.description: Get pricing info for a model Output: JSON with pricing details

llm_list_models.description: List all supported models Output: JSON array of model names

llm_truncate_to_tokens.description: Truncate text to fit within a token limit Strategies: head   - Keep first N tokens (default) tail   - Keep last N tokens middle - Keep start and end, cut middle Output: Truncated text

llm_split_chunks.description: Split text into token-sized chunks Options: --overlap N      Overlap N tokens between chunks (default: 0) --preserve-lines Try to split at line boundaries Output: JSON array of chunks with metadata

llm_split_chunks_file.description: Split a file into token-sized chunks Output: JSON array of chunks

llm_context_window.description: Get context window size for a model Output: integer max tokens

llm_fits_context.description: Check if text fits in model's context window

llm_model_family.description: Get model family from model name Output: "gpt-4" or "claude-3" etc.

llm_count_tokens_usop.description: USOP-compliant token count Output: JSON envelope with token count

llm_truncate_usop.description: USOP-compliant truncation Output: JSON envelope with truncated text and metadata

log.description: Production-grade logging with JSON output, log levels, context fields, timing, and rotation helpers

log::set_level.signature: log::set_level "debug"  # debug, info, warn, error, fatal

log::set_format.description: Set output format Note: This overrides MAINFRAME_OUTPUT. To use MAINFRAME_OUTPUT, call log::sync_with_mainframe_output

log::sync_with_mainframe_output.description: Sync format with MAINFRAME_OUTPUT environment variable

log::fatal.description: Fatal level logging (also exits with code 1)

log::json.description: Emit JSON log with explicit level
log::json.signature: log::json "info" "User logged in" user_id=123 ip="1.2.3.4" action="login"

log::time_start.description: Start a timer for an operation

log::time.description: Time a command and log its duration

log::rotate.description: Rotate log file if it exceeds max size

log::needs_rotation.description: Check if rotation is needed (without rotating)

log::fail.description: Log an error and return error code (doesn't exit like fatal)

log::child.description: Create a child logger with additional context $mylog "User authenticated"  # includes service and component

mcp_server.description: MCP server implementation that exposes Mainframe functions as tools for Claude Code and other MCP-compatible clients. Enables AI assistants to discover and invoke Mainframe capabilities through standardized JSON-RPC interface.

meta.description: Variable introspection, dynamic calls, namerefs, constants

var_get.description: Get variable value by name (indirect expansion)
var_get.signature: var_get "varname" result_var  (no subshell, stores in result_var)

var_exists.description: Check if variable is set (may be empty)

var_nonempty.description: Check if variable is set and non-empty

vars_with_prefix.description: Get all variable names matching prefix Populates result_array with matching variable names

vars_matching.description: Get all variable names matching pattern (glob)

var_is_assoc.description: Check if variable is associative array

const_default.description: Define constant if not already set

func_source.description: Get function source file and line (if available)

var_ref.description: Create a nameref to a variable Note: Creates global nameref; useful in functions

method_exists.description: Check if method exists for prefix

call_or_default.description: Call function if exists, otherwise return default

metrics.description: Pure bash implementation of Prometheus-style metrics including counters, gauges, histograms, and summaries with label support. Exports to Prometheus text exposition format, JSON, and OpenMetrics.

metric_labels_format.description: Format labels string from key=value pairs

metrics_register.description: Register a metric with the registry. All metrics must be registered before use. Re-registering with the same type is allowed, different type raises error.

metrics_unregister.description: Unregister a metric and remove all its data.

metrics_get.description: Get a metric's type and help by name.

metrics_clear.description: Clear all registered metrics and their values.

counter_create.description: Create a counter metric. Counters can only increase (monotonically).

counter_add.description: Add a value to a counter. Value must be non-negative.

counter_get.description: Get the current value of a counter.

counter_reset.description: Reset a counter to 0 (mainly for testing purposes). Note: In production, counters should not be reset as this breaks rate calculations.

counter_labels.description: Create a counter with label support.
counter_labels.signature: counter_labels "http_requests_total" "method status" "Total HTTP requests by method and status"

gauge_create.description: Create a gauge metric. Gauges can go up and down.

gauge_set.description: Set a gauge to a specific value.

gauge_add.description: Add a value to a gauge (can be negative).

gauge_sub.description: Subtract a value from a gauge.

gauge_get.description: Get the current value of a gauge.

gauge_labels.description: Create a gauge with label support.

histogram_create.description: Create a histogram metric with specified buckets. Buckets define the upper bounds for observation counting.

histogram_observe.description: Record an observation in a histogram.

histogram_get_buckets.description: Get all bucket counts for a histogram.

histogram_get_sum.description: Get the sum of all observed values for a histogram.

histogram_get_count.description: Get the total count of observations for a histogram.

histogram_labels.description: Create a histogram with label support.

histogram_quantile.description: Estimate a quantile from histogram buckets using linear interpolation. Note: This is an approximation, not exact quantile calculation.

summary_create.description: Create a summary metric for calculating streaming quantiles. Note: Summary stores raw observations with timestamps for sliding window.

summary_observe.description: Record an observation in a summary.

summary_get_quantiles.description: Get quantile values from a summary.

summary_get_sum.description: Get the sum of all observations in a summary.

summary_get_count.description: Get the total count of observations in a summary.

timer_start.description: Start a timer for measuring duration. Returns a timer ID to pass to timer_stop.

timer_stop.description: Stop a timer and record the duration to the associated metric.

timer_observe.description: Directly observe a pre-calculated duration (no timer needed).

metric_timestamp.description: Get current timestamp formatted for metric export.

metrics_export_prometheus.description: Export all metrics in Prometheus text exposition format. Compatible with Prometheus scraping.

metrics_export_json.description: Export all metrics in JSON format.

metrics_export_openmetrics.description: Export all metrics in OpenMetrics format (Prometheus 2.0+). OpenMetrics is a CNCF standard that extends Prometheus format.

metrics_push_gateway.description: Push all metrics to a Prometheus Pushgateway.

metrics_serve.description: Start a simple HTTP server that serves metrics. Uses netcat for pure bash HTTP server capability. Press Ctrl+C to stop.

metrics_update_process.description: Create and update standard process metrics (Go/Python client compatibility).

metrics_measure.description: Measure and record the execution time of a function.

metrics_init.description: Initialize the metrics system with an optional prefix. All metric names will be prefixed with this value.

metrics_counter_inc.description: Increment a counter metric. Counters can only increase; use gauges for values that can decrease.

metrics_counter_get.description: Get the current value of a counter.

metrics_gauge_set.description: Set a gauge to a specific value. Gauges can go up and down, unlike counters.

metrics_gauge_inc.description: Increment a gauge by a value (default: 1).

metrics_gauge_dec.description: Decrement a gauge by a value (default: 1).

metrics_gauge_get.description: Get the current value of a gauge.

metrics_histogram_observe.description: Record an observation in a histogram. Histograms track the distribution of values using configurable buckets.

metrics_summary_observe.description: Record an observation in a summary. Summaries calculate quantiles over a sliding time window.

metrics_export.description: Export all metrics in Prometheus text format.

metrics_push.description: Push all metrics to a Prometheus Pushgateway.

netscan.description: Pure-bash network utilities for port checking, host discovery, banner grabbing, and HTTP header extraction. Designed for defensive administration and AI-automated infrastructure checks.

port_check.description: Check if a TCP port is open on a host. Uses /dev/tcp first, falls back to nc/ncat if available.

host_alive.description: Check if a host is alive using ping (ICMP) or TCP fallback.

banner_grab.description: Grab the service banner from an open port. Connects and reads the first response line (useful for SSH, SMTP, FTP, etc.).

http_headers.description: Extract HTTP response headers from a URL. Uses curl if available, falls back to /dev/tcp for HTTP (not HTTPS).

monitor_port.description: Check port state and return structured JSON result. Useful for watchdog scripts and monitoring loops.

scan_range.description: Scan a host for open ports from a list or range. Returns JSON array of results.

parse_nmap.description: Parse nmap greppable output (-oG) into structured JSON. Each host becomes a JSON object with IP, hostname, and open ports.

observe.description: Trace, timing, and structured error reporting that produces JSON output AI coding assistants can parse for debugging, error recovery, and performance analysis.

trace_start.description: Begin a named trace. Returns a trace ID that must be passed to trace_step and trace_end. Captures start timestamp. State is stored in files to survive subshell boundaries.

trace_step.description: Record a step within an active trace. Each step has a name, optional status, and optional detail message.

trace_end.description: End a trace and emit a complete JSON summary including all steps, duration, and final status.

observe_command.description: Execute a command and capture its stdout, stderr, exit code, and duration as a structured JSON object. Useful for AI agents to understand command outcomes without parsing unstructured output.

stack_trace.description: Capture the current bash call stack as a JSON array. Each frame includes function name, source file, and line number. Useful for error reporting that AI agents can parse.

observe_error.description: Emit a structured error with code, message, function context, and stack. Designed for AI agents to parse and take corrective action.

observe_time.description: Get current timestamp suitable for duration calculations. Uses EPOCHREALTIME (bash 5.0+) or date fallback.

observe_elapsed.description: Calculate elapsed time between a start timestamp and now.

otel_trace_start.description: Start a new trace with W3C trace context. Optionally accepts JSON attributes for the root span.

otel_trace_end.description: End the current trace. If trace_id is provided, ends that specific trace. Otherwise uses the current trace context.

otel_span_create.description: Create a span within the current trace. If parent_id is not provided, uses the current span as parent.

otel_span_end.description: End a span with optional status code. Status can be "OK", "ERROR", or "UNSET".

otel_span_attribute.description: Add a key-value attribute to a span. Value type is auto-detected (string, number, boolean).

otel_span_event.description: Add a timestamped event to a span. Events represent discrete occurrences during span execution.

otel_span_exception.description: Record an exception in a span. Sets span status to ERROR.

otel_traceparent.description: Get the W3C traceparent header value for the current context. Format: version-trace_id-span_id-flags

otel_tracestate.description: Get the W3C tracestate header value for the current context. Contains vendor-specific trace information.

otel_parse_traceparent.description: Parse an incoming traceparent header and populate environment variables.

otel_context_inject.description: Propagate trace context to child processes via environment variables. Call before spawning subprocesses to maintain trace continuity.

otel_context_extract.description: Extract trace context from environment variables. Call at the start of child processes to continue the trace.

otel_export_otlp.description: Export all collected spans to an OTLP HTTP endpoint. Uses /dev/tcp for pure bash HTTP or falls back to curl.

otel_export_json.description: Export all spans to a JSON file for debugging or batch processing.

otel_export_console.description: Export spans to console as structured JSON log lines. Useful for debugging and development.

otel_flush.description: Flush any pending/buffered spans. Should be called before process exit to ensure all spans are exported.

otel_instrument.description: Auto-instrument a function call with span creation/completion. Wraps function execution with span lifecycle management.

otel_timed.description: Measure execution time with automatic span creation.

otel_batch_start.description: Start batch collection mode for efficiency. Spans are buffered and exported together.

otel_batch_add.description: Add a span JSON to the batch buffer. Internal use primarily, but can be used for custom span formats.

otel_batch_flush.description: Flush all buffered spans to the configured exporter.

otel_from_trace.description: Bridge function to convert a legacy MAINFRAME trace to OTEL format. Allows gradual migration from trace_* to otel_* functions.

optimize.description: Detect and suggest optimizations for shell commands and pipelines Eliminates useless use of cat, consolidates grep chains, and more.

optimize_command.description: Suggest optimized version of a command with full details

optimize_pipeline.description: Optimize a pipeline with multiple stages
optimize_pipeline.signature: optimize_pipeline "cat big.txt | head -100 | tail -10 | grep foo"

optimize_check.description: Check if a command can be optimized

orchestrate.description: Manages teams of Claude Code agents working in coordinated TMUX windows. Provides team lifecycle, agent spawning, inter-agent communication via Redis pub/sub, task distribution, and centralized state management.

otel.description: W3C Trace Context compliant distributed tracing for bash scripts. Provides span creation, context propagation, and multi-format export.

otel_init.description: Initialize the OpenTelemetry tracer Options: --service NAME     Service name for traces (default: mainframe) --endpoint URL     OTLP HTTP endpoint (default: http://localhost:4318) --sample-rate N    Sampling rate 0.0-1.0 (default: 1.0)

otel_trace_add_event.description: Add an event to the current span

otel_trace_set_attribute.description: Set an attribute on the current span

otel_inject_headers.description: Get headers for context propagation (W3C format)

otel_timed.description: Time a command with automatic span

output.description: Enables all MAINFRAME functions to output structured JSON envelopes instead of raw text, making the toolkit machine-readable for AI coding agents. Provides mode detection, envelope functions, timing helpers, and the output_wrap meta-wrapper.

output_init.description: Initialize output system Sets default mode if not already set via environment

output_mode.description: Get or set output mode Without args: returns current mode With arg: sets mode if valid, returns 1 if invalid

output_is_json.description: Check if JSON output mode is active Returns 0 if MAINFRAME_OUTPUT=json

output_is_raw.description: Check if raw output mode is active Returns 0 if MAINFRAME_OUTPUT=raw or unset

output_is_minimal.description: Check if minimal output mode is active Returns 0 if MAINFRAME_OUTPUT=minimal

output_is_debug.description: Check if debug output mode is active Returns 0 if MAINFRAME_OUTPUT=debug

output_format.description: Returns the current output format (backward compat alias)

output_timer_elapsed.description: Get elapsed time since timer_start in milliseconds Returns 0 if timer was not started

output_success.description: Emit a success envelope Format depends on MAINFRAME_OUTPUT mode: raw:     plain data json:    {"ok":true,"data":"...","meta":{...},"hint":"..."} minimal: {"ok":true,"data":"..."} debug:   json + timestamp + caller

output_error.description: Emit an error envelope Format depends on MAINFRAME_OUTPUT mode: raw:     plain message to stderr json:    {"ok":false,"error":{"code":"...","msg":"...","suggestion":"..."}} minimal: {"ok":false,"error":{"code":"...","msg":"..."}} debug:   json + timestamp + caller

output_raw.description: Emit raw text regardless of output mode Always bypasses envelope formatting

output_json.description: Emit JSON string unchanged regardless of output mode Useful for custom JSON that shouldn't be wrapped

output_json_object.description: Emit JSON object data (already formatted JSON)

output_json_array.description: Emit JSON array data (already formatted JSON)

output_wrap.description: Wrap any function call with automatic USOP envelope Captures stdout, exit code, and timing

output_with_mode.description: Execute command with temporary output mode Restores original mode after execution

output_success_legacy.description: Legacy output_success (old format) Kept for backward compatibility with existing code

output_json_string_kv.description: Emit a JSON key-value pair with string value Output: "key":"value"

output_json_number.description: Emit a JSON key-value pair with number value Output: "key":42

output_json_bool.description: Emit a JSON key-value pair with boolean value Output: "key":true

output_json_null.description: Emit a JSON key-value pair with null value Output: "key":null

output_json_array_from_lines.description: Read stdin lines and output a JSON array of strings Output: ["line1","line2"]

output_list.description: Emit a list/array envelope (legacy format) Output: {"status":"success","data":["item1","item2","item3"],"count":3}

output_object.description: Emit a key-value object envelope (legacy format)

output_progress.description: Emit a progress envelope for streaming/long operations

mainframe_call.description: Invoke any MAINFRAME function with automatic USOP wrapping Captures stdout, stderr, exit code, and wraps in JSON envelope

output_auto.description: Auto-detect output mode and emit appropriate format (legacy)

output_structured_error.description: Create a rich error object with context for AI agent consumption

output_try.description: Wrap a command and produce structured error on failure

usop_exec.description: Execute any command and wrap result in USOP envelope Returns JSON with: success, exit_code, stdout, stderr, duration_ms, command, cwd, timestamp

usop_get.description: Parse USOP result and extract a specific field Supports both top-level fields and nested values

usop_ok.description: Check if USOP result indicates success Returns 0 (true) if success:true, 1 (false) otherwise

usop_read_file.description: Read file and return USOP envelope with content Includes file metadata (size, path) and AI-friendly error suggestions

usop_write_file.description: Write content to file atomically and return USOP envelope Uses atomic_write if available for safe file operations

usop_delete_file.description: Delete a file and return a USOP envelope describing the result.

usop_file_read.description: Compatibility wrappers for older USOP file helper names.

usop_list_dir.description: List directory contents and return USOP envelope Returns array of entries with file/directory information

usop_run_background.description: Run command in background and return USOP envelope with tracking info Returns PID and paths to stdout/stderr capture files

usop_check_pid.description: Check status of a process by PID Returns running status and exit code if completed

usop_error_command_failed.description: Generate command failed error envelope with full context
examples: usop_error_command_failed "git pull" "128" "fatal: not a git repository"

usop_exec_v.description: Execute command and store USOP result in variable (avoids subshell)

usop_get_v.description: Extract USOP field into variable (avoids subshell)

usop_result.description: usop_result - Enhanced result with status and typed data

parallel_v2.description: Enhanced parallel execution with map/reduce patterns, progress tracking, and multiple execution backends (GNU parallel,  background jobs, or sequential fallback).

parallel_v2_map.description: Map a command over a list of files/items

parallel_v2_reduce.description: Reduce a list of files/items using a binary operation

parallel_v2_pipeline.description: Pipeline: run commands in sequence with parallel stages

parallel.description: High-level parallel execution patterns for AI agent workflows. Provides map, race, all, any, batch, and retry operations with USOP-compliant JSON output and progress reporting.

parallel_map.description: Apply function to each item in parallel

parallel_race.description: First to complete wins, cancel others

parallel_all.description: Wait for all, return all results

parallel_batch.description: Process in batches with optional concurrency per batch

parse_output.description: Structured JSON parsing of common tool outputs. Eliminates per-agent regex hacking of compiler and test runner output.

parse_detect_format.description: Detect what kind of output this is Reads stdin, outputs format name

parse_output.description: Parse output with format auto-detection or explicit format

parse_failures_only.description: Extract just the failures/errors from parsed output Reads parse_output JSON from stdin, outputs only failures array

parse_error_count.description: Count total errors across parsed output Reads stdin, outputs integer

parse_is_success.description: Check if output indicates success (0 failures) Reads stdin, returns 0 if no failures

parse_summary.description: Format parsed output as human-readable summary Reads parsed JSON from stdin, outputs 1-2 line summary

parse_locations.description: Extract file:line references from parsed output (for editor integration) Reads stdin, outputs "file:line" pairs (one per line)

parsers.description: Pure-bash parsers for common formats: CSV, key-value configs, INI files, URLs, and semantic versions. All output JSON for AI agent consumption.

parse_csv_line.description: Parse a single CSV line into the global array PARSE_CSV_FIELDS. Handles quoted fields with commas and escaped quotes. Uses a global array to avoid subshell overhead.

parse_csv_json.description: Parse a CSV line and return as JSON array.

parse_key_value.description: Parse key-value pairs from input. Supports = and : separators, strips whitespace, ignores comments (# and ;) and blank lines.

parse_ini.description: Parse an INI file into nested JSON. Sections become top-level keys, with key-value pairs as nested objects.

parse_url.description: Parse a URL into its components: scheme, user, password, host, port, path, query, fragment. Returns a JSON object.

parse_semver.description: Parse a semantic version string into its components. Supports: major.minor.patch[-prerelease][+build]

semver_compare.description: Compare two semantic versions. Returns: -1 if v1 < v2 0 if v1 == v2 1 if v1 > v2

path.description: Cross-platform path operations without external tools

path_normalize.description: Normalize path by resolving . and .. and collapsing multiple slashes

path_absolute.description: Get absolute path (resolves to real filesystem path)

path_relative.description: Get relative path from base to target

path_to_unix.description: Convert Windows path to Unix path

path_to_windows.description: Convert Unix path to Windows path

path_quote.description: Quote path for safe shell usage

path_is_safe.description: Check if path is safe (no directory traversal outside base)

path_ensure_dir.description: Ensure parent directory exists (create if needed) Creates: /foo/bar/baz/

path_common_prefix.description: Find common prefix of multiple paths

path_has_parent_ref.description: Check if path contains parent reference (..)

path_is_hidden.description: Check if path is hidden (starts with .)

path_equals.description: Check if two paths are equivalent (after normalization)

path_split.description: Split path into array of components

path_resolve.description: Resolve symlinks to get real path

perf.description: Bash version detection, feature gating for modern Bash (5.0+/5.3+), and performance measurement utilities. Enables conditional use of fast-path features (namerefs, EPOCHREALTIME, current-shell subst) while maintaining Bash 4.0+ compatibility.

bash_version.description: Get the current Bash version as a dot-separated string.

bash_version_major.description: Get just the major version number.

bash_version_at_least.description: Check if the current Bash version is at least the specified version.

bash_has_feature.description: Check if a specific Bash feature is available. Features: - namerefs: declare -n (Bash 4.3+) - mapfile: mapfile/readarray builtin (Bash 4.0+) - associative_arrays: declare -A (Bash 4.0+) - epochrealtime: $EPOCHREALTIME variable (Bash 5.0+) - epochseconds: $EPOCHSECONDS variable (Bash 5.0+) - wait_n: wait -n for any child (Bash 4.3+) - lastpipe: shopt -s lastpipe (Bash 4.2+) - globasciiranges: shopt -s globasciiranges (Bash 4.3+) - inherit_errexit: shopt -s inherit_errexit (Bash 4.4+) - extglob: extended globbing (Bash 4.0+)

bash_features.description: List all known features and whether they're available. Returns a JSON object for AI agent consumption.

perf_timer_start.description: Start a named performance timer. Uses variable storage to avoid subshells. The timer value is stored in a global variable PERF_TIMER_<name>.

perf_timer_elapsed.description: Stop a named timer and print the elapsed duration in seconds.

perf_timer_stop.description: Stop a named timer and emit a JSON timing result.

perf_compare.description: Compare execution time of two commands/approaches. Runs each command N iterations and reports average times.

perf_setvar.description: Set a variable by name without subshell. Uses printf -v which is significantly faster than var=$(command) for simple assignments. This is a thin wrapper for documentation/discoverability.

perf_capture.description: Capture command output into a variable using lastpipe (avoids subshell for the reader). Falls back to $() on older Bash.

perf_benchmark.description: Benchmark a single command with iteration count. Returns JSON with total time, average, and iterations.

pipe_map.description: Apply a function/command to each line echo -e "foo\nbar" | pipe_map upper  # uses MAINFRAME upper() Security: Commands are validated for dangerous patterns before execution

pipe_filter.description: Filter lines matching a pattern (grep-like) echo -e "1\n2\n3" | pipe_filter '^[12]$'

pipe_reject.description: Filter lines NOT matching a pattern

pipe_reduce.description: Reduce/fold stream to single value Security: Expression is validated for dangerous patterns

mainframe_context_require.description: Require that the current context matches the expected profile. Useful as a guard at the top of production-only or development-only scripts.

safewrap_policy.description: Set the wrapping policy level which controls block/confirm thresholds. strict:     block >= 5, confirm >= 3 moderate:   block >= 7, confirm >= 5 permissive: block >= 9, confirm >= 7

streaming.description: Functional stream processing primitives for AI agent workflows. Provides map, filter, reduce, parallel processing, rate limiting, type-aware pipes, and USOP-compliant JSON output.

stream_map.description: Apply function to each line of input

stream_reduce_v.description: Reduce with nameref output (no subshells for iteration)

stream_take.description: Take first N items from stream

stream_skip.description: Skip first N items from stream

stream_chunk.description: Split stream into chunks of N lines

stream_fanout.description: Fan out stream to multiple processors
stream_fanout.signature: cat data.txt | stream_fanout 3 proc1 proc2 proc3

stream_any.description: Check if any line matches predicate
stream_any.signature: cat file.txt | stream_any is_error && echo "found errors"

stream_all.description: Check if all lines match predicate
stream_all.signature: cat file.txt | stream_all is_valid && echo "all valid"

stream_none.description: Check if no lines match predicate
stream_none.signature: cat file.txt | stream_none is_empty && echo "no empty lines"

stream_tap.description: Tap into stream for side effects

streams.description: Lazy, composable stream processing using pipes and process substitution. Provides functional primitives (map, filter, reduce, etc.) for declarative data transformation pipelines.

stream_from_array.description: Create a stream from an array. Elements are output one per line. Supports both nameref and positional arguments.
examples: local arr=(a b c); stream_from_array arr

stream_from_file.description: Create a stream from file lines. Empty lines are preserved.

stream_from_command.description: Create a stream from command output. Each line of output becomes an element.

stream_from_range.description: Create a numeric range stream. Similar to Python's range() or seq.

stream_from_generator.description: Create a stream from a generator function. The generator is called repeatedly and should output one element per call. Return non-zero to signal end.

stream_empty.description: Create an empty stream. Useful as identity element for stream operations.

stream_of.description: Create a stream from positional arguments. Each argument becomes one element.

stream_repeat.description: Create a stream that repeats a value N times.
examples: stream_repeat "x" 5  # outputs: x x x x x (one per line)

stream_iterate.description: Create an infinite stream by repeatedly applying a function to previous value. IMPORTANT: Use stream_take to limit output!

stream_map.description: Transform each element using a function or expression. The current element is available as $item in the expression.

stream_filter.description: Filter elements that match a predicate. The current element is $item. The predicate should return exit code 0 for elements to keep.

stream_take.description: Take only the first N elements from the stream.

stream_drop.description: Skip the first N elements from the stream.

stream_take_while.description: Take elements while the predicate returns true. Stops at first false.

stream_drop_while.description: Skip elements while the predicate returns true. Output starts at first false.

stream_distinct.description: Remove duplicate elements from the stream. First occurrence is kept. Note: Requires full materialization for tracking seen elements.
examples: stream_of a b a c b d | stream_distinct  # a, b, c, d

stream_sorted.description: Sort elements. Supports numeric and lexicographic sorting. Note: Requires full materialization.

stream_reversed.description: Reverse the order of elements. Note: Requires full materialization.
examples: stream_of a b c | stream_reversed  # c, b, a

stream_flat_map.description: Map each element to zero or more elements, then flatten the result. Transform should output zero, one, or more lines.

stream_enumerate.description: Add index to each element. Output format: "index:element" or custom format.

stream_compact.description: Filter out empty lines and lines containing only whitespace.

stream_reduce.description: Reduce stream to a single value. First element is initial accumulator. Use stream_fold for custom initial value.

stream_fold.description: Fold stream with an initial accumulator value.

stream_count.description: Count the number of elements in the stream.

stream_sum.description: Sum numeric elements in the stream.

stream_min.description: Find the minimum value in the stream. Supports numeric and string comparison.

stream_max.description: Find the maximum value in the stream. Supports numeric and string comparison.

stream_first.description: Get the first element from the stream.
examples: stream_of a b c | stream_first  # a

stream_last.description: Get the last element from the stream. Note: Requires full materialization.
examples: stream_of a b c | stream_last  # c

stream_any.description: Check if any element matches the predicate.

stream_all.description: Check if all elements match the predicate. Empty stream returns true.

stream_none.description: Check if no elements match the predicate.

stream_window.description: Create sliding windows of fixed size over the stream. Each window is output as a JSON array.

stream_batch.description: Create fixed-size batches (non-overlapping windows). Last batch may be smaller than size.

stream_buffer.description: Buffer elements until a condition is met, then flush.
examples: stream_of a b END c d END | stream_buffer '[[ "$item" == "END" ]]'

stream_throttle.description: Rate-limit stream output. Minimum delay between elements.

stream_debounce.description: Debounce rapid items - only emit after quiet period. Emits the last value seen after delay_ms of no new input.
examples: (echo a; sleep 0.01; echo b; sleep 0.5; echo c) | stream_debounce 100

stream_sample.description: Sample every Nth element from the stream.

stream_random.description: Get a random element from the stream using reservoir sampling.

stream_shuffle.description: Shuffle elements randomly. Note: Requires full materialization.
examples: stream_of a b c d | stream_shuffle

stream_merge.description: Merge multiple streams, interleaving their output. Reads from all streams in round-robin fashion.

stream_zip.description: Zip two streams together. Stops when either stream ends.
examples: stream_zip <(stream_of a b c) <(stream_of 1 2 3)  # a:1, b:2, c:3
stream_concat <(stream_of a b) <(stream_of c d)  # a, b, c, d

stream_interleave.description: Interleave multiple streams, taking one element from each in turn.

stream_merge_sorted.description: Merge two sorted streams maintaining sort order.

stream_collect.description: Collect stream elements into an array.

stream_to_file.description: Write stream elements to a file.

stream_foreach.description: Execute an action for each element. Does not transform the stream. The action can use $item for the current element.

stream_to_json.description: Output stream as a JSON array with proper escaping.

stream_tee.description: Tee stream to a file while passing through to stdout. Like Unix tee but for streams.
examples: stream_of a b c | stream_tee /tmp/log.txt | stream_map 'echo "Got: $item"'

stream_to_lines.description: Output stream elements separated by newlines (identity operation). Useful for explicit pipeline termination.

stream_join.description: Join all elements into a single line with delimiter.
examples: stream_of a b c | stream_join ","  # a,b,c

stream_peek.description: Debug helper - prints each element to stderr while passing through.

stream_require_non_empty.description: Assert stream is non-empty. Fails (returns 1) if no elements.

stream_count_tap.description: Count elements while passing stream through.

stream_of a b c d | stream_at 2  # c

stream_group_by.description: Group elements by a key extractor.
examples: stream_of aa ab ba bb | stream_group_by 'echo ${item:0:1}'

stream_frequency.description: Count frequency of each unique element.
examples: stream_of a b a c b a | stream_frequency

stream_partition.description: Partition elements into two groups based on predicate.

stream_chunk_by.description: Split stream into chunks at separator elements. Separator elements are not included in output.
examples: stream_of a b --- c d --- e | stream_chunk_by '---'

stream_difference.description: Compute set difference (elements in first stream not in second).
examples: stream_of a b c d | stream_difference <(stream_of b d)  # a, c

stream_intersect.description: Compute set intersection (elements in both streams).
examples: stream_of a b c d | stream_intersect <(stream_of b d e)  # b, d

stream_union.description: Compute set union (all unique elements from both streams).
examples: stream_of a b c | stream_union <(stream_of b c d)  # a, b, c, d

stream_pipe.description: Compose multiple stream operations into a single pipeline. Each argument is a stream operation to apply in sequence.

stream_version.description: Get stream library version and info.

tirith_ecosystem.description: Detects supply chain risks in package management, container registries, Git repositories, and Web3 endpoints.

tirith_check_docker_registry.description: tirith_check_docker_registry CMD [SOURCE] Detect docker pull, docker run, or FROM in Dockerfiles using untrusted container registries. Docker Hub images without a registry prefix (e.g. nginx:latest) are considered safe. Severity: medium | Rule: DockerUntrustedRegistry

tirith_check_pip_url_install.description: tirith_check_pip_url_install CMD [SOURCE] Detect pip install from URLs rather than PyPI. Flags direct URL installs (https://, http://, git+https://) and --index-url pointing to non-PyPI domains. Normal PyPI installs (pip install package-name) are not flagged. Severity: medium | Rule: PipUrlInstall

tirith_check_npm_url_install.description: tirith_check_npm_url_install CMD [SOURCE] Detect npm install from URLs or git repos. Flags direct URL installs (https://..., git+..., github:user/repo) and npm config set registry pointing to non-standard registries. Normal npm installs are not flagged. Severity: medium | Rule: NpmUrlInstall

tirith_check_web3_rpc.description: tirith_check_web3_rpc CMD [SOURCE] Detect hardcoded Web3 RPC endpoints in commands. Looks for URLs containing known web3 provider domains and common RPC path patterns with hex API keys. Severity: low | Rule: Web3RpcEndpoint

tirith_check_web3_address.description: tirith_check_web3_address CMD [SOURCE] Detect Ethereum-style addresses (0x followed by 40 hex chars) in commands. This is informational -- flags hardcoded blockchain addresses. Severity: low | Rule: Web3AddressInUrl

tirith_check_git_typosquat.description: tirith_check_git_typosquat CMD [SOURCE] Detect git clone with potentially typosquatted repository names. Extracts org/repo from the clone URL and compares against popular repos using levenshtein_distance from fuzzy.sh. Flags repos with edit distance 1-2 from a popular repo (close but not exact match). Severity: medium | Rule: GitTyposquat

tirith_scan_ecosystem.description: tirith_scan_ecosystem CMD [SOURCE] Run all 6 ecosystem security checks on the input command.

tirith_hook.description: Installs a bash DEBUG trap that intercepts commands before execution, running tirith security scans. Chains with existing DEBUG traps rather than replacing them. Supports bypass via TIRITH=0 prefix.

tirith_hook_install.description: tirith_hook_install Install the tirith preexec hook using the bash DEBUG trap. Chains with any existing DEBUG trap rather than replacing it.

tirith_hook_uninstall.description: tirith_hook_uninstall Remove the tirith preexec hook and restore the original DEBUG trap.

tirith_hook_status.description: tirith_hook_status Print the current hook status.

tirith_hook_toggle.description: tirith_hook_toggle Toggle the hook on/off without installing/uninstalling the trap.

tirith_inject.description: Detects terminal injection attacks including ANSI escape sequences, BiDi control characters, zero-width characters, and hidden multiline commands.

tirith_check_ansi_escapes.description: tirith_check_ansi_escapes INPUT [SOURCE] Detect ANSI escape sequences that could manipulate terminal display. Checks for CSI (\x1b[), 8-bit CSI (\x9b), OSC (\x1b]), SS2 (\x1bN), and SS3 (\x1bO) sequences. Severity: high | Rule: AnsiEscapes

tirith_check_control_chars.description: tirith_check_control_chars INPUT [SOURCE] Detect ASCII control characters that should not appear in normal input. Checks for \x00-\x08 and \x0e-\x1f, excluding tab (\x09), newline (\x0a), and carriage return (\x0d) which are legitimate whitespace. Severity: high | Rule: ControlChars

tirith_check_bidi_controls.description: tirith_check_bidi_controls INPUT [SOURCE] Detect Unicode BiDi (bidirectional) control characters that can reorder displayed text to hide malicious code (CVE-2021-42574, "Trojan Source"). Severity: critical | Rule: BidiControls

tirith_check_zero_width.description: tirith_check_zero_width INPUT [SOURCE] Detect zero-width Unicode characters that can hide content or alter string comparisons without visible change. Severity: high | Rule: ZeroWidthChars

tirith_check_hidden_multiline.description: tirith_check_hidden_multiline INPUT [SOURCE] Detect hidden newlines or carriage returns that conceal additional commands within a seemingly single-line input. Only flags when a newline is followed by a dangerous command keyword. Severity: high | Rule: HiddenMultiline

tirith_scan_injection.description: tirith_scan_injection INPUT [SOURCE] Run all 5 injection detection rules on the input.

tirith_strip_dangerous_chars.description: tirith_strip_dangerous_chars INPUT Strip BiDi controls, zero-width characters, and control characters (keeping tab, newline, and carriage return) from the input. Output: Cleaned string on stdout

tirith_path.description: Detects suspicious path patterns including non-ASCII characters, homoglyph substitutions, and double-encoding attacks.

tirith_pipe.description: Detects dangerous pipe-to-shell patterns, dotfile overwrites, and unsafe archive extraction commands.

tirith_url.description: Detects URL-based attacks including homograph/confusable domains, punycode tricks, userinfo deception, plain HTTP to sensitive endpoints, URL shorteners, and insecure TLS configurations.

tirith_check_non_ascii_hostname.description: tirith_check_non_ascii_hostname URL [SOURCE] Detect hostnames containing non-ASCII characters (potential homograph attack)

tirith_check_punycode_domain.description: tirith_check_punycode_domain URL [SOURCE] Detect punycode-encoded hostname labels (xn-- prefix)

tirith_check_mixed_script.description: tirith_check_mixed_script URL [SOURCE] Detect hostname labels that mix ASCII letters with non-ASCII confusable chars

tirith_check_userinfo_trick.description: tirith_check_userinfo_trick URL [SOURCE] Detect user:pass@host pattern that disguises the real destination e.g. http://google.com@evil.com/path looks like google.com but goes to evil.com

tirith_check_invalid_host_chars.description: tirith_check_invalid_host_chars URL [SOURCE] Detect characters that should not appear in hostnames

tirith_check_trailing_dot_whitespace.description: tirith_check_trailing_dot_whitespace URL [SOURCE] Detect trailing dots or whitespace in hostname that could confuse DNS resolution

tirith_check_confusable_domain.description: tirith_check_confusable_domain URL [SOURCE] Detect domains that look like well-known domains via confusable characters Uses skeleton comparison and Levenshtein distance (if fuzzy.sh loaded)

tirith_check_raw_ip_url.description: tirith_check_raw_ip_url URL [SOURCE] Detect URLs that use raw IP addresses instead of hostnames

tirith_check_non_standard_port.description: tirith_check_non_standard_port URL [SOURCE] Flag URLs with ports other than 80 (http) or 443 (https)

tirith_check_lookalike_tld.description: tirith_check_lookalike_tld URL [SOURCE] Check if TLD is a lookalike that impersonates file extensions

tirith_check_plain_http.description: tirith_check_plain_http URL [SOURCE] Flag plain HTTP URLs that point to sensitive sinks (login, auth, payment, etc.)

tirith_check_schemeless.description: tirith_check_schemeless URL [SOURCE] Flag URLs without scheme (e.g. //evil.com/login) pointing to sensitive sinks

tirith_check_shortened_url.description: tirith_check_shortened_url URL [SOURCE] Detect URLs using known URL shortener domains

tirith_check_insecure_tls.description: tirith_check_insecure_tls CMD [SOURCE] Check command string for insecure TLS flags that disable certificate validation

tirith_scan_url_checks.description: tirith_scan_url_checks URL [SOURCE] Run all URL security checks against a URL

tirith.description: Aggregates all tirith_* security libraries into a unified scanning interface. Provides URL trust scoring, JSONL audit logging, configuration loading, and reporting.

tirith_init.description: tirith_init Initialize the tirith subsystem: set up shared state, load config. Safe to call multiple times (idempotent).

tirith_load_config.description: tirith_load_config [FILE] Load tirith configuration from a YAML-like file. Format: version: 1 fail_mode: open allowlist: - *.trusted.com - github.com blocklist: - evil.com severity_overrides: RawIpUrl: low ShortenedUrl: high

tirith_check_proxy_env.description: tirith_check_proxy_env [SOURCE] Check if proxy environment variables are set, which could redirect traffic. Severity: low | Rule: ProxyEnvSet

tirith_scan_command.description: tirith_scan_command CMD [SOURCE] Full security scan of a shell command string. Runs injection, pipe, path, URL, and ecosystem checks.

tirith_scan_url.description: tirith_scan_url URL [SOURCE] Full security scan of a single URL.

tirith_scan_input.description: tirith_scan_input TEXT [SOURCE] Scan arbitrary text for injection attacks.

tirith_url_trust_score.description: tirith_url_trust_score URL Calculate a trust score for a URL on a 0-100 scale. Higher score = more trustworthy. Output: Integer score on stdout

tirith_audit_log.description: tirith_audit_log CMD RESULT [EXTRA] Append a JSONL entry to the audit log.

tirith_clear.description: tirith_clear Reset all findings and counters.

tirith_has_findings.description: tirith_has_findings [SEVERITY] Check if there are any findings, optionally of a specific severity.

tirith_should_block.description: tirith_should_block Determine if current findings warrant blocking execution. In "closed" mode: block on HIGH or CRITICAL In "open" mode: block only on CRITICAL
